ruleName: Ball Deflected by Person Attending or Holding Up Flagstick or Anything Else
title: Replacing the Flag during a Putt in Match Play
question: In match play, Rachel deliberately replaces the flagstick in the hole while Mark is putting. Mark’s putt is then deflected by the flagstick. What is the ruling?
explanation: Under Rule 11.8, in match play, if a player deliberately takes an action to affect a ball in motion (for example, replacing the flagstick while an opponent’s ball is rolling towards the hole), they lose the hole.

juniorVersion.title: Putting and the Flag in a Match
juniorVersion.question: Rachel and Mark are playing a match. While Mark is trying to putt, Rachel puts the flagstick back in the hole on purpose. Mark’s ball then hits the flagstick. What happens?
juniorVersion.explanation: If you put the flagstick back in the hole on purpose while your friend’s ball is rolling, and the ball then hits the flagstick, you lose that hole in match play.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The tall stick that goes in the hole to show where it is on the green.
A game of golf where you try to win more holes than your friend, not count all your shots for the whole round.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind children to wait until everyone has finished putting before touching the flagstick, so no one is distracted or gets in trouble.
likelyMisconceptions: It’s okay to put the flag back while someone is putting if you think it will help them.
Nothing happens if the ball hits the flag after you put it back during someone else’s putt.
